messages:
sam: quick sync — noticed Dedicated pools sometimes trigger a model-fallback path that blows our p50 latency. thinking we need to clearly split responsibility between routing (which picks model/region) and the autoscaler/operator (which ensures capacity). any objections to that boundary?
jane: +1 to a clean contract. how do we signal SLOs? currently routing just has a boolean "latency_preference" and backend picks best model. thats too coarse.
kai: agree — we should surface explicit SLO tuples (latency_ms, pctile) in the request metadata. router uses that to pick candidate models/tiers; autoscaler uses it to set warmup headroom/priority.
maria: question: if router picks a cheaper model but autoscaler can't warm nodes in time, who should trigger fallback to hosted or higher tier? router or operator?
sam: that's the heart of it. i propose router must never assume capacity — it picks ranked candidates and includes a contract header: "candidates: [m1:latency:50, m2:latency:150]". then autoscaler evaluates admission and either accepts (reserve) or returns "rejection-with-reason" quickly. router retries the next candidate on rejection. simplifies decisions.
jane: that sounds reasonable. the API contract needs a fast rejection path (<50ms) to keep tail low. otherwise router blocking is the problem.
kai: implementation sketch: 
```
# candidate header pseudo
X-Model-Candidates: [{"id":"redwood-ggml-1","slop":50},{"id":"open-4b-q","slop":150}]
X-SLO: {"p50_ms":60}
```
autoscaler response: ACCEPT|DEFER|REJECT + optional ETA (for DEFER).
maria: DEFER with ETA is nice — router can decide to wait small ETA or immediately move to next candidate. suggest max-wait threshold per caller (default 200ms).
sam: operationally we need operator metrics for DEFER frequency per tenant + per model. if DEFER spikes => trigger prewarm policy or rollout throttling.
kai: also think autoscaler needs to expose a lightweight query API: /admit?candidates=... returns token if accepted. token carries reservation TTL. router attaches token on actual request.
jane: token TTL prevents double-counting. also lets operator reclaim if not used. we should define token semantics: non-blocking reservation vs provisional warmup ticket.
maria: edge-case: burst lane. when a tenant has burst credits, admission should bypass soft headroom but still return an admit token so billing/accounting works.
sam: good point — policy must include "bypass_level" in response. otherwise people will try to cheat.
deploy-bot: deployment: autoscaler-v2 will add /admit and token; rollout in canary first. note: requires minor protobuf change in router->control plane header. :rocket:
jane: rollout plan idea — 1) router sends raw SLO header only (no tokens) and we log what autoscaler WOULD have done for 2 weeks. 2) enable /admit in canary for internal tenants. 3) open to small set of customers. 4) full rollout. this gives us a guardrail.
kai: monitoring: track admit_latency, admit_reject_rate, defer_eta_histogram, token_miss_rate. add alert when reject_rate > 1% for high-tier tenants.
maria: action items: sam to draft API header + token semantics doc. kai to stub /admit proto and perf budget. jane to add rollout checklist and canary test plan. i'll add monitoring panels.
sam: agreed. i'll post an RFC follow-up with concrete header shape and example flows. thanks all. :thumbsup:
